advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Count children with a non-None ticket_id (mirror child_closure_findings' skip) instead of len(children) in build_child_closure_evidence.
evidence: completion.py:261 `total = len(children)`
completion.py:167-168 in child_closure_findings: `cid = c.get("ticket_id")` then `if cid is None: continue`
docstring completion.py:246 `Reuses the same child enumeration ... so the counts stay consistent`
completion.py:276 `f"{total - len(unc_ids)} of {total} direct child ticket(s) are closed AND certified;`
advisory.finding: build_child_closure_evidence reports total=len(children) (all rows returned by list_tickets), but child_closure_findings excludes children whose ticket_id is None; a None-id child therefore inflates the reported total and makes the derived 'closed AND certified' count (total - len(unc_ids)) overstate certified children, contradicting the docstring's claim that counts stay consistent with child_closure_findings.
scenarios: A child ticket lacking a ticket_id key is returned by list_tickets: it is silently dropped by child_closure_findings but counted in build_child_closure_evidence's total, so the evidence block claims more certified children than were actually proven.
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute total = sum(1 for c in children if c.get("ticket_id") is not None) so the total matches child_closure_findings' effective enumeration.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pass the already-enumerated child list (or its count) from child_closure_findings into build_child_closure_evidence rather than re-reading list_tickets.
evidence: completion.py:134 child_closure_findings: `children = _reads.list_tickets(parent=ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)`
completion.py:258 build_child_closure_evidence: `children = _reads.list_tickets(parent=ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)`
gate_ops.py:77 `blocking, uncertified = child_closure_findings(canonical, ctx.repo_root)` then gate_ops.py:190 `child_evidence = build_child_closure_evidence(canonical, ctx.repo_root, uncertified)`
docstring completion.py:246 claims it 'Reuses the same child enumeration'
advisory.finding: build_child_closure_evidence re-calls _reads.list_tickets(parent=ticket_id) even though child_closure_findings already enumerated the same children moments earlier in the same precheck; this is a redundant store read and opens a consistency window where the two enumerations can disagree (the docstring says it 'reuses the same child enumeration' but it re-enumerates).
scenarios: Two separate reads of the child set within one gate op; if the store mutates between them (or a transient read differs) the reported total diverges from the proof the short-circuit used.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where _reads.list_tickets raises, asserting build_child_closure_evidence returns "" and no child-closure block appears in the fenced context.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/completion.py:257-260: `try: children = _reads.list_tickets(...) except Exception: return ""`
The test _patch helper always sets list_tickets to a non-raising lambda; no test configures it to raise.
ABSENCE: no test asserts build_child_closure_evidence returns "" (nor that completion_precheck omits the block) when child enumeration fails.
advisory.finding: The read-error branch of build_child_closure_evidence (list_tickets raising -> returns "") is untested. The docstring asserts this contract ('when enumeration fails' returns "") and it mirrors child_closure_findings' own read-error arm, but no test injects an exception from _reads.list_tickets, so a regression that re-raised (crashing the close gate) or emitted a partial block from an unread child set would go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that monkeypatches _reads.list_tickets to raise and asserts build_child_closure_evidence('T-1', None, []) == '' and 'direct child' not in completion_precheck(...)['context'].

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that _uncertified_child_ids skips the read-error marker finding ('direct children of ... could not be certified') and correctly extracts ids from per-child findings.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/completion.py:230-232: `parts = str(f.get("criterion","")).split(); if len(parts)>=3 and parts[0]=="direct" and parts[1]=="child": ids.append(parts[2])`
src/rebar/llm/completion.py:224-227: docstring asserts the read-error marker 'carries no id and is skipped'

ABSENCE: tests only call build_child_closure_evidence indirectly with well-formed per-child uncertified findings; none pass a marker-shaped finding to verify it is skipped, and _uncertified_child_ids is never unit-tested directly.
advisory.finding: The _uncertified_child_ids parser's handling of the read-error marker finding is untested. The function's docstring claims the marker (criterion 'direct children of ... could not be certified') 'carries no id and is skipped' — relying on parts[1] being 'children' not 'child'. This fragile string-split contract has a real branch (len(parts)>=3 and parts[0]=='direct' and parts[1]=='child') that no test exercises with a marker-shaped finding, so a change to either the marker phrasing or the criterion format could silently mis-parse ids without any test failing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with >=2 closed-but-uncertified children asserting both ids appear and the certified/uncertified counts are correct.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/completion.py:275-278: `f"{total - len(unc_ids)} of {total} ... are closed but NOT certified: {', '.join(unc_ids)}."`
tests/unit/workflow/test_child_closure_evidence_6ec8.py: `assert len(uncertified) == 1` — the sole else-branch test has one uncertified id.
ABSENCE: no test with two or more closed-but-uncertified children asserting both ids appear and the count reads e.g. '1 of 3 ... the following 2 are closed but NOT certified'.
advisory.finding: The multiple-uncertified-ids path (the ', '.join(unc_ids) branch with more than one uncertified child) is untested. The only test that reaches the else-branch has exactly one uncertified child (C-force), so the count arithmetic (`{total - len(unc_ids)} of {total}`) and the comma-join of multiple ids are never exercised for len>1, leaving off-by-one/format regressions undetected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the child-closure evidence block tamper-evident against forged copies in untrusted ticket text (e.g. emit it in the TRUSTED prompt region, or bind it with a per-run nonce the verifier must match) so the verifier's no-tool-call authority cannot be triggered by attacker-authored ticket content.
evidence: operations.py:108: `blocks = [_format_ticket(ticket)]` — the `base` context inside the same fence is rendered from ticket fields (title/description/comments) that non-privileged actors can author.

completion_verifier.md:157-158: 'You MAY rely on that block to resolve a criterion of the form "every child is closed / certified" WITHOUT making a tool call.' — the trusted prompt grants authority keyed only to the `## Deterministic child-closure evidence` header, which is forgeable within untrusted ticket text.

REACHABILITY BOUND: the deterministic short-circuit for an UNCLOSED child is unchanged (gate_ops.py:107-126; test_unclosed_child_short_circuits_no_llm), so a forged block cannot force closure over a genuinely-open child; the residual exposure is the LLM-judged certification half and epic ACs resolved from the block.
advisory.finding: A trusted verifier-prompt caveat grants the LLM authority to resolve 'every child closed/certified' criteria WITHOUT a tool call by relying on a `## Deterministic child-closure evidence` block, but that block is injected INSIDE the `<untrusted_ticket_context>` fence alongside attacker-influenceable ticket title/description/comment text, distinguished only by its markdown header — so a forged block in ticket content could induce the verifier to treat a child-closure criterion as MET / certifiable.
scenarios: An epic whose completion criteria include 'every child story is closed/certified'; an attacker (or a low-privilege ticket author) embeds a forged `## Deterministic child-closure evidence` block claiming all children are closed & certified in the epic's description or a comment, inducing the verifier to mark the criterion MET without a tool call.
